title: Playback States, Cascade Layers, Typed attr(), Border Beam & Screen Palette
description: Five browser-native patterns: real media playback-state pseudo-classes, a draggable cascade-layer stack, typed attr() styling, a spinning border-beam, and a real EyeDropper color picker.

drops.title: Now Playing
drops.description: Three synthesized audio players whose glyphs and shimmer react to real playback-state pseudo-classes.
drops.concept: CSS Selectors Level 4 introduces :playing, :paused, :seeking, :buffering, :muted, and :volume-locked pseudo-classes that match <audio>/<video> elements by their live playback state, letting @keyframes react without any timeupdate/waiting event JS. Since native support is still rolling out, this drop mirrors the same states via real media events into data-state attributes so the demo works everywhere while showing exactly what the pure-CSS selectors would target.
drops.source: CSS Selectors Level 4 spec + web-platform-tests interop issue #510

drops.title: Cascade Layer Stack
drops.description: Reorder four CSS cascade layers and watch a card repaint instantly — priority comes from layer order, not specificity.
drops.concept: A single @layer reset, theme, components, overrides; statement fixes cascade-layer priority by declaration order, regardless of where each layer's rule body appears in the file. Rewriting just that one statement's text at runtime re-resolves which of four equally-weak-selector layers wins for the same card, and a toggle demonstrates that any unlayered rule always outranks every layered one.

interaction.mouse: Click the up/down arrows to reorder layers
interaction.touch: Same arrow buttons work via tap

drops.title: Attribute-Driven Type
drops.description: Drag a slider and only an HTML data-attribute changes — attr() type() parses it straight into typed CSS.
drops.concept: The upgraded attr() function now accepts a type() hint — attr(data-size type(<length-percentage>)), attr(data-tint type(<color>)) — usable on any CSS property, not just content, so the browser parses an HTML attribute's string value into a real typed CSS value with zero element.style writes. A CSS custom-property fallback line keeps the demo working identically in browsers that don't yet resolve the enhancement path.
drops.source: Chrome for Developers Blog — "CSS attr() gets an upgrade"

interaction.mouse: Drag sliders and the color swatch to restyle the headline live

drops.title: Border Beam
drops.description: A thin arc of light continuously chases each card's rounded border — pure CSS, compositor-only.
drops.concept: An oversized conic-gradient rotated via an animated @property --beam-angle is masked with mask-composite: exclude down to just the border-width ring of a rounded card, so only a traveling arc of light is visible rather than a full spinning gradient. Because only the custom property changes per frame, the effect runs on the compositor with no layout or paint cost, and four instances show different durations, widths, colors, and directions plus a live-tunable fifth.

interaction.mouse: Drag the panel dials to reshape the live card's beam
interaction.touch: Panel hides on mobile; other three cards still animate

drops.title: Screen Palette
drops.description: A color-picker component built on the real EyeDropper API — sample any pixel on your entire screen.
drops.concept: window.EyeDropper lets a page open the OS-level color-sampling cursor and read back any pixel on the user's screen, not just within the page's own canvas. This drop wraps it in a small palette-builder component with a live WCAG contrast-ratio readout against white and black text, persists picks to localStorage, and falls back to a native <input type="color"> in browsers where EyeDropper isn't available.
